glossary.oedema: Swelling from fluid collecting in the tissues.
glossary.subcutaneous tissue: The fatty layer beneath the skin.
glossary.lymphatic: Relating to the lymph vessels that drain excess tissue fluid.
glossary.capillary: The tiniest blood vessels, where oxygen passes to the tissues.
glossary.leg ulcer: A wound on the leg that has not healed within about two weeks.
glossary.obesity: Excess body fat, usually a BMI of 30 or more.
glossary.immobility: Being unable to move much, which stops the calf pump.
glossary.exudative: Producing lots of fluid from the wound.
glossary.irregular edges: Uneven, sloping ulcer margins typical of venous ulcers.
glossary.night cramps: Painful muscle spasms in the legs at night.
glossary.non-healing: Failing to heal despite treatment, usually over weeks.
glossary.systemic illness: Being unwell throughout the body, for example fever and tachycardia.
glossary.arterial compromise: Reduced arterial blood supply to the limb.
glossary.peripheral pulses: Pulses felt in the limbs, such as dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial.
glossary.compression therapy: Bandages or stockings that squeeze the leg to push blood back towards the heart.
glossary.leg elevation: Raising the legs above the heart to help venous drainage.
glossary.recurrence: The condition coming back after healing.
glossary.laser therapy: Using laser heat inside the vein to close it.
glossary.non-compressible: Arteries too stiff to squeeze shut with a cuff, falsely raising ABPI.
glossary.vascular surgery: Surgical specialty treating arteries and veins.
glossary.penicillin-allergic: Allergic to penicillin antibiotics such as flucloxacillin.
glossary.valvular incompetence: Failure of vein valves to close, letting blood flow backwards.
glossary.outflow obstruction: Blockage of venous drainage, for example from an old DVT.
glossary.inflammation: The body's response to injury: redness, swelling, heat and pain.
glossary.pigmentation: Colouring of the skin, here brown from haemosiderin.
glossary.venous return: Blood flow back to the heart through the veins.
